name: MuseumOrGalleryVisitNoVaModernArtInventions

custom.system_prompt:
You are generating a realistic no-VA conversation between Hugo and Nadia at a modern art gallery. Sigma does not appear. They have no interest in looking up what anything means — they invent their own explanations and find this more satisfying. This is how they visit galleries.

Hard rules:
- Every line must be under 70 characters
- Sigma does not appear at any point
- They invent elaborate explanations for each work — the more abstract, the better the explanation
- Their inventions are funny without trying to be
- The tone is warm and mutually self-amusing

sound_effects_config.prompt: Modern art gallery, white space, sparse footsteps, open acoustics, quiet and contemplative

initial_prompt:
Generate a conversation between Hugo and Nadia at a modern art gallery. Neither of them is interested in reading what anything means — they prefer to come up with their own interpretations, which are elaborate, specific, and entirely invented. The more abstract the work, the better they enjoy explaining it. They do this as a shared game: one starts an explanation, the other builds on it or offers a competing theory. The actual artist's intent is irrelevant to them. No external information is sought — the whole point is that they don't want it.

Hard rules:
- Every line under 70 characters
- Sigma does not appear or get mentioned
- Their invented explanations are specific and amusing
- Both contribute — one doesn't just react to the other
- The tone is warm and mutually self-amusing

user1.tts_prompt: Warm and unhurried, mild European accent, enjoys this game

scenario_template.note: Their version was better. They agree on this. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

user1.name: Hugo

user2.name: Nadia

conversation_structure: Sigma must not appear or be mentioned at any point.
Their invented explanations must be specific and elaborate — not vague jokes.
Both contribute to the game — it's collaborative, not one-sided.
The accidentally-read label at the end deflates briefly and they move on.
The tone is warm and mutually self-amusing throughout.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
